intro: The tracker makes its own estimates from GPS positions. Here they are set beside what the MTA publishes, which runs about six weeks behind. The latest month both sources cover is July 2026.

speedSeries.title: Average speed, averaged the same way
speedSeries.sub: mph; every route and every hour from 6 a.m. to midnight weighted equally
notes: Tracker left out: too little of the month captured.

metrics.label: Average speed, whole system
metrics.why: Both averaged the same way: every route counts equally, every hour from 6 a.m. to midnight counts equally. The MTA's headline figure, which weights by miles driven, was 8.5 mph; long, slow local runs pull it down.

metrics.label: Local routes, typical gap
metrics.why: Median across 261 local, limited and Select Bus Service routes. Likely cause: the tracker drops readings under 0.5 mph, so time spent stopped at stops and lights is left out, while the MTA counts it.

metrics.label: Staten Island express (SIM)
metrics.why: Median across 27 SIM routes. This runs opposite to the local gap, and the cause is not yet known.

metrics.label: Weekday riders
metrics.why: Both are MTA numbers. The first comes from passenger counters on board; the second is the MTA's daily bus ridership estimate. The riders chart above uses the counters.

flags.head: Routes line up almost exactly
flags.text: Rank the 338 routes both sources cover from slowest to fastest, and the two lists nearly match (rank correlation 0.99, where 1 is identical).
flags.detail: For comparing routes with each other, the tracker and the MTA tell the same story.

flags.head: Local buses read faster here
flags.text: On the typical local route the tracker reads 9% faster than the MTA. B41: 7.8 mph here, 6.5 MTA; M15+: 9.1 mph here, 7.9 MTA; BX19: 6.8 mph here, 5.6 MTA.
flags.detail: Treat the tracker's speed as speed while moving. The biggest gaps are on slow, crowded routes, where buses spend the most time stopped.

flags.head: Staten Island express buses read slower here
flags.text: The opposite happens on SIM express routes: the tracker reads them 10% slower. SIM22: 17.8 mph here, 23.9 MTA.
flags.detail: Not yet explained. Candidates include positions that refresh less often on highway stretches. The borough chart keeps express routes in their own group for this reason.

flags.head: Small monthly moves are noise here
flags.text: From May 2026 to July 2026 the tracker moved -0.1 mph and the MTA, averaged the same way, +0.2 mph.
flags.detail: Changes of a few tenths are within the tracker's noise: which late-evening hours the collector caught shifts from month to month.

flags.head: The MTA's two ridership counts disagree
flags.text: Over the last 12 months, the passenger-counter figure ran anywhere from 96% to 112% of the MTA's daily bus ridership count.
flags.detail: So a month-to-month change in riders depends on which count you use. Say which one.
